title: A panel must not give focus back to an opener that can disappear while it is open
rule: When a drawer or popover gives focus back on close to the element that opened it, and that opener can be hidden or removed while the panel is open (a '+N' chip that goes when everything fits, a row action on a row that leaves the list), open the panel with focus on a control that always stays, such as the bar's main button. focus() on a hidden element does nothing, so focus falls to body and the next Tab starts at the top of the page. Test it with a Playwright step that opens the panel by keyboard, makes the opener go away, closes with Escape and asserts where focus is, and check that the test fails without the fix.
rationale: E41.4 (#450): the +N chip opened the filter drawer; turning filters off from the drawer hid +N, and Escape left focus on body.
